To: Supply Chain Leadership
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Date: Today
Subject: Balancing Shipping Cost and Carbon with Real-World Operating Limits

Context
Our distribution network ships products from multiple warehouses to multiple stores. Every warehouse-to-store route carries two performance signals: monetary cost per unit and carbon emissions per unit. In practice, the lowest-cost lanes frequently have higher emissions, creating a direct trade-off between financial efficiency and our sustainability commitments. We need a practical, defensible plan that meets service needs while aligning with our cost and environmental priorities.

Operational Rules We Must Honor
- Setup/activation costs for routes: Turning on a new shipping lane entails a one-time setup charge (e.g., carrier contracting, customs paperwork, dock configuration). A route is either active or not; if we activate it, we incur the full setup cost regardless of how much we ship.
- Minimum order quantities on active lanes: Activated lanes must move at least a defined minimum number of units to justify fixed handling and equipment. Partial truckloads are not accepted on these routes; once a lane is on, shipments must meet or exceed the minimum.
- Limit on suppliers per store: To protect receiving capacity and keep vendor management manageable, each store may be served by no more than a preset number of warehouses. This encourages consolidation and service reliability at the dock.

Supply and Demand Boundaries
- Warehouse inventory limits: Shipments from each warehouse cannot exceed available inventory for the planning period.
- Store demand requirements: Each store’s minimum demand must be fully covered within the period; shortfalls are not acceptable.

Management Priority
Leadership has defined relative importance weights for cost and emissions. These weights will be applied to the variable (per-unit) shipping costs and the total emissions, respectively. The one-time setup costs for any activated routes are added in full and are not scaled by the weights. This ensures we reflect both ongoing per-unit efficiency and our entry costs for opening lanes.

Goal
Identify which routes to activate and how much to ship on each route so that:
- Warehouse inventory is not exceeded and every store’s demand is met,
- Activated routes meet their minimum order thresholds,
- Each store is served by no more than the allowed number of warehouses,
- The combined outcome balances what we spend and what we emit: variable shipping costs weighted by our cost priority, total emissions weighted by our emissions priority, plus unweighted setup costs for any lanes we activate.

Outcome and Next Steps
We will assemble a recommended shipping plan that lists the active lanes, volumes by route, and the resulting total cost and emissions under the stated priorities and operating rules. We will also prepare scenario views to illustrate how the plan shifts as management adjusts the cost-versus-emissions weights or the supplier cap per store. Upon approval, we will align with carriers and warehouse teams to implement the selected routes and volumes for the upcoming period.
